From 55e03b8cbe2783ec9acfb88e8adb946ed504e117 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Darrick J. Wong" <djwong@kernel.org>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 09:27:40 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] xfs: check for deleted cursors when revalidating two btrees

The free space and inode btree repair functions will rebuild both btrees
at the same time, after which it needs to evaluate both btrees to
confirm that the corruptions are gone.

However, Jiaming Zhang ran syzbot and produced a crash in the second
xchk_allocbt call.  His root-cause analysis is as follows (with minor
corrections):

 In xrep_revalidate_allocbt(), xchk_allocbt() is called twice (first
 for BNOBT, second for CNTBT). The cause of this issue is that the
 first call nullified the cursor required by the second call.

 Let's first enter xrep_revalidate_allocbt() via following call chain:

 xfs_file_ioctl() ->
 xfs_ioc_scrubv_metadata() ->
 xfs_scrub_metadata() ->
 `sc->ops->repair_eval(sc)` ->
 xrep_revalidate_allocbt()

 xchk_allocbt() is called twice in this function. In the first call:

 /* Note that sc->sm->sm_type is XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_BNOPT now */
 xchk_allocbt() ->
 xchk_btree() ->
 `bs->scrub_rec(bs, recp)` ->
 xchk_allocbt_rec() ->
 xchk_allocbt_xref() ->
 xchk_allocbt_xref_other()

 since sm_type is XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_BNOBT, pur is set to &sc->sa.cnt_cur.
 Kernel called xfs_alloc_get_rec() and returned -EFSCORRUPTED. Call
 chain:

 xfs_alloc_get_rec() ->
 xfs_btree_get_rec() ->
 xfs_btree_check_block() ->
 (XFS_IS_CORRUPT || XFS_TEST_ERROR), the former is false and the latter
 is true, return -EFSCORRUPTED. This should be caused by
 ioctl$XFS_IOC_ERROR_INJECTION I guess.

 Back to xchk_allocbt_xref_other(), after receiving -EFSCORRUPTED from
 xfs_alloc_get_rec(), kernel called xchk_should_check_xref(). In this
 function, *curpp (points to sc->sa.cnt_cur) is nullified.

 Back to xrep_revalidate_allocbt(), since sc->sa.cnt_cur has been
 nullified, it then triggered null-ptr-deref via xchk_allocbt() (second
 call) -> xchk_btree().

So.  The bnobt revalidation failed on a cross-reference attempt, so we
deleted the cntbt cursor, and then crashed when we tried to revalidate
the cntbt.  Therefore, check for a null cntbt cursor before that
revalidation, and mark the repair incomplete.  Also we can ignore the
second tree entirely if the first tree was rebuilt but is already
corrupt.

Apply the same fix to xrep_revalidate_iallocbt because it has the same
problem.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-xfs/CANypQFYU5rRPkTy=iG5m1Lp4RWasSgrHXAh3p8YJojxV0X15dQ@mail.gmail.com/T/#m520c7835fad637eccf843c7936c200589427cc7e
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v6.8
Fixes: dbfbf3bdf639a2 ("xfs: repair inode btrees")
Signed-off-by: "Darrick J. Wong" <djwong@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Tested-by: Jiaming Zhang <r772577952@gmail.com>

diff --git a/fs/xfs/scrub/alloc_repair.c b/fs/xfs/scrub/alloc_repair.c
index f9a9b4327189..5b4c2a39a155 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/scrub/alloc_repair.c
+++ b/fs/xfs/scrub/alloc_repair.c
@@ -923,7 +923,22 @@ xrep_revalidate_allocbt(
 	if (error)
 		goto out;
 
+	/*
+	 * If the bnobt is still corrupt, we've failed to repair the filesystem
+	 * and should just bail out.
+	 *
+	 * If the bnobt fails cross-examination with the cntbt, the scan will
+	 * free the cntbt cursor, so we need to mark the repair incomplete
+	 * and avoid walking off the end of the NULL cntbt cursor.
+	 */
+	if (sc->sm->sm_flags & XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT)
+		goto out;
+
 	sc->sm->sm_type = XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_CNTBT;
+	if (!sc->sa.cnt_cur) {
+		xchk_set_incomplete(sc);
+		goto out;
+	}
 	error = xchk_allocbt(sc);
 out:
 	sc->sm->sm_type = old_type;

diff --git a/fs/xfs/scrub/ialloc_repair.c b/fs/xfs/scrub/ialloc_repair.c
index d206054c1ae3..9b63b9d19e1b 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/scrub/ialloc_repair.c
+++ b/fs/xfs/scrub/ialloc_repair.c
@@ -863,10 +863,24 @@ xrep_revalidate_iallocbt(
 	if (error)
 		goto out;
 
-	if (xfs_has_finobt(sc->mp)) {
-		sc->sm->sm_type = XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_FINOBT;
-		error = xchk_iallocbt(sc);
+	/*
+	 * If the inobt is still corrupt, we've failed to repair the filesystem
+	 * and should just bail out.
+	 *
+	 * If the inobt fails cross-examination with the finobt, the scan will
+	 * free the finobt cursor, so we need to mark the repair incomplete
+	 * and avoid walking off the end of the NULL finobt cursor.
+	 */
+	if (!xfs_has_finobt(sc->mp) ||
+	    (sc->sm->sm_flags & XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT))
+		goto out;
+
+	sc->sm->sm_type = XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_FINOBT;
+	if (!sc->sa.fino_cur) {
+		xchk_set_incomplete(sc);
+		goto out;
 	}
+	error = xchk_iallocbt(sc);
 
 out:
 	sc->sm->sm_type = old_type;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

### Modifications

**`fs/xfs/scrub/alloc_repair.c`**:
- After the first `xchk_allocbt()` call (for the bnobt), added two checks before the second call (for the cntbt):
  1. If the bnobt scan already marked the scrub as corrupt (`XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT`), bail out immediately – no point in trying the cntbt.
  2. If the cntbt cursor (`sc->sa.cnt_cur`) was nullified during the bnobt cross‑reference (e.g., due to a failed `xfs_alloc_get_rec()`), mark the repair as incomplete and skip the cntbt scan to avoid a null‑pointer dereference.

**`fs/xfs/scrub/ialloc_repair.c`**:
- Similar changes for the inode btree pair (inobt + finobt):
  - Bail out if the inobt scan already found corruption or if the finobt is not present on the filesystem.
  - Before the finobt scan, check if the finobt cursor (`sc->sa.fino_cur`) was nullified during inobt cross‑referencing; if so, mark incomplete and skip.

### Relationships

Both modifications address the same underlying pattern: a `xrep_revalidate_*` function calls two btree validation routines in sequence. The first validation may corrupt‑check the second tree via cross‑referencing, and if that cross‑reference fails (e.g., `-EFSCORRUPTED`), the second tree’s cursor is freed and set to `NULL`. The second validation then attempts to use that null cursor and crashes. The fix in each file guards against this by:
1. Aborting early if the first tree is already corrupt (avoid pointless work).
2. Checking whether the second tree’s cursor survived the first validation, and if not, skipping the second scan and marking the repair as incomplete.

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a crash in XFS's btree repair revalidation logic when both trees in a pair (free space: BNOBT/CNTBT; inode: INOBT/FINOBT) are being revalidated sequentially. The root cause is that the first btree revalidation (e.g., BNOBT) may nullify the cursor required for the second (CNTBT) via a failed cross-reference check, causing a null-pointer dereference. The fix adds safeguard checks before the second revalidation call.

### Changes in `fs/xfs/scrub/alloc_repair.c` (`xrep_revalidate_allocbt()`):
1. After revalidating the BNOBT (first call to `xchk_allocbt`), check if the BNOBT itself is still marked corrupt (`XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT`). If so, bail out immediately without attempting CNTBT revalidation.
2. If BNOBT is not corrupt, check whether the CNTBT cursor (`sc->sa.cnt_cur`) has been nullified (e.g., due to an error in cross-referencing during BNOBT revalidation). If null, mark the repair as incomplete (`xchk_set_incomplete`) and skip the CNTBT revalidation.
3. Only proceed to call `xchk_allocbt` for CNTBT if the cursor is valid.

### Changes in `fs/xfs/scrub/ialloc_repair.c` (`xrep_revalidate_iallocbt()`):
1. After revalidating the INOBT (first call to `xchk_iallocbt`), check if the INOBT is still corrupt. If so, bail out.
2. If the filesystem has a free inode B-tree (FINOBT) and INOBT is not corrupt, check whether the FINOBT cursor (`sc->sa.fino_cur`) has been nullified. If null, mark repair incomplete and skip FINOBT revalidation.
3. Only call `xchk_iallocbt` for FINOBT if the cursor is non-null.

### Relationship Between Modifications:
Both modifications follow the identical pattern to handle the same class of bug: after the first btree in a pair is revalidated, a null cursor for the second tree (resulting from a cross-reference failure during the first revalidation) is detected and handled by marking the repair incomplete, preventing a null-pointer dereference. The early exit on corruption of the first tree also avoids pointless work. The fix ensures robustness for both the free space and inode btree repair paths.

Here is the commit message:
xfs: check for deleted cursors when revalidating two btrees

The free space and inode btree repair functions will rebuild both btrees
at the same time, after which it needs to evaluate both btrees to
confirm that the corruptions are gone.

However, Jiaming Zhang ran syzbot and produced a crash in the second
xchk_allocbt call.  His root-cause analysis is as follows (with minor
corrections):

 In xrep_revalidate_allocbt(), xchk_allocbt() is called twice (first
 for BNOBT, second for CNTBT). The cause of this issue is that the
 first call nullified the cursor required by the second call.

 Let's first enter xrep_revalidate_allocbt() via following call chain:

 xfs_file_ioctl() ->
 xfs_ioc_scrubv_metadata() ->
 xfs_scrub_metadata() ->
 `sc->ops->repair_eval(sc)` ->
 xrep_revalidate_allocbt()

 xchk_allocbt() is called twice in this function. In the first call:

 /* Note that sc->sm->sm_type is XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_BNOPT now */
 xchk_allocbt() ->
 xchk_btree() ->
 `bs->scrub_rec(bs, recp)` ->
 xchk_allocbt_rec() ->
 xchk_allocbt_xref() ->
 xchk_allocbt_xref_other()

 since sm_type is XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_BNOBT, pur is set to &sc->sa.cnt_cur.
 Kernel called xfs_alloc_get_rec() and returned -EFSCORRUPTED. Call
 chain:

 xfs_alloc_get_rec() ->
 xfs_btree_get_rec() ->
 xfs_btree_check_block() ->
 (XFS_IS_CORRUPT || XFS_TEST_ERROR), the former is false and the latter
 is true, return -EFSCORRUPTED. This should be caused by
 ioctl$XFS_IOC_ERROR_INJECTION I guess.

 Back to xchk_allocbt_xref_other(), after receiving -EFSCORRUPTED from
 xfs_alloc_get_rec(), kernel called xchk_should_check_xref(). In this
 function, *curpp (points to sc->sa.cnt_cur) is nullified.

 Back to xrep_revalidate_allocbt(), since sc->sa.cnt_cur has been
 nullified, it then triggered null-ptr-deref via xchk_allocbt() (second
 call) -> xchk_btree().

So.  The bnobt revalidation failed on a cross-reference attempt, so we
deleted the cntbt cursor, and then crashed when we tried to revalidate
the cntbt.  Therefore, check for a null cntbt cursor before that
revalidation, and mark the repair incomplete.  Also we can ignore the
second tree entirely if the first tree was rebuilt but is already
corrupt.

Apply the same fix to xrep_revalidate_iallocbt because it has the same
problem.

Here is the root cause:
In xrep_revalidate_allocbt(), the first call to xchk_allocbt() for the BNOBT may trigger a cross-reference check via xchk_allocbt_xref_other() that fails (e.g., due to an injected error returning -EFSCORRUPTED). This failure invokes xchk_should_check_xref(), which nullifies the CNTBT cursor pointer (sc->sa.cnt_cur). The revalidation function then proceeds to call xchk_allocbt() a second time for the CNTBT without checking if the cursor is NULL, leading to a null-pointer dereference when xchk_btree() attempts to use it. The same logic flaw exists in xrep_revalidate_iallocbt() for the finobt cursor. The patch fixes both by adding early exits when the first btree remains corrupt or when the second tree's cursor has been nullified.

Here is the patch:
 /* Make sure both btrees are ok after we've rebuilt them. */
 int
 xrep_revalidate_allocbt(
 	struct xfs_scrub	*sc)
 {
 	__u32			old_type = sc->sm->sm_type;
 	int			error;
 
 	/*
 	 * We must update sm_type temporarily so that the tree-to-tree cross
 	 * reference checks will work in the correct direction, and also so
 	 * that tracing will report correctly if there are more errors.
 	 */
 	sc->sm->sm_type = XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_BNOBT;
 	error = xchk_allocbt(sc);
 	if (error)
 		goto out;
 
+	/*
+	 * If the bnobt is still corrupt, we've failed to repair the filesystem
+	 * and should just bail out.
+	 *
+	 * If the bnobt fails cross-examination with the cntbt, the scan will
+	 * free the cntbt cursor, so we need to mark the repair incomplete
+	 * and avoid walking off the end of the NULL cntbt cursor.
+	 */
+	if (sc->sm->sm_flags & XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT)
+		goto out;
+
 	sc->sm->sm_type = XFS_SCRUB_TYPE_CNTBT;
+	if (!sc->sa.cnt_cur) {
+		xchk_set_incomplete(sc);
+		goto out;
+	}
 	error = xchk_allocbt(sc);
 out:
 	sc->sm->sm_type = old_type;
 	return error;
 }
